findings.title: Public findMany method removed without migrating callers
findings.body: The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously queried BookingTimeStatusDenormalized with the authorization and filter conditions, and replaces it with getBaseConditions returning only a Prisma.Sql fragment. No caller is updated in this PR, so any existing consumer calling service.findMany(...) will fail TypeScript compilation and lose the previous query behavior (including merging caller-supplied where/select arguments). Migrate all call sites to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions in the same change, or keep a compatible findMany wrapper.

findings.title: OR authorization/filter fragments are returned without outer parentheses
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return fragments such as (A AND B) OR (C AND D) with no enclosing parentheses, buildFilterConditions similarly returns an unparenthesized eventType OR at line 106, and getBaseConditions returns these fragments unwrapped when only one kind of condition exists. Because AND binds tighter than OR in SQL, a caller composing the public result as WHERE ${conditions} AND <date or status condition> will apply the extra condition only to the last OR branch; the first team-booking branch will ignore it, returning rows outside the requested range/filter. Wrap each top-level returned condition in parentheses so the fragments are safely composable.

findings.title: Team/org ANY(array) SQL is never executed against the database
findings.body: The team-scope (line 278) and org-scope (line 305) tests only assert equality between two locally constructed Prisma.sql objects. The sole executed $queryRaw test at line 481 uses user scope, which contains no array parameter. Therefore the new "teamId" = ANY(${number[]}) and "userId" = ANY(${number[]}) parameter binding is never verified against PostgreSQL; if Prisma/Postgres cannot infer or encode the JS array parameter for these queries, both scopes fail at runtime while all tests pass. Add executed $queryRaw integration tests for team and org scopes asserting the returned booking ids.

findings.title: Caching tests were deleted while caching logic remains
findings.body: This PR removes the entire Caching describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions calls reuse cached results, but InsightsBookingService still maintains cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions state. No replacement test covers the cached paths, including the cached null filter case, so a regression in cache initialization or invalidation would go undetected. Restore the caching tests adapted to compare Prisma.Sql results instead of Prisma where-objects.
